title: Heart Disease Deaths Have Fallen 50% Since 1990 — Most of What's Left Is Preventable
hook: Coronary artery disease deaths have been cut in half over three decades, but a new analysis says nearly 90% of the deaths that remain trace back to risk factors we already know how to manage.
key_points: Deaths from coronary (ischemic) heart disease fell more than 50% in the U.S. between 1990 and 2023.
Despite that progress, 88.8% of the roughly 473,000 coronary artery disease deaths in 2023 were linked to modifiable risk factors.
Smoking-related deaths dropped 33.3% and particulate air pollution deaths fell 74.9% over the same period.
But some risk factors moved the wrong way: deaths tied to high BMI rose 12.5%, and deaths tied to high blood glucose rose 10.5%.
The leading modifiable risk factors behind 2023 deaths were high blood pressure (47.2%), poor diet (38.6%), and high LDL cholesterol (28.5%).
content_html: Coronary artery disease deaths in the U.S. have fallen by more than half since 1990 — real progress against the country's leading killer. A new analysis argues most of what's left is still within reach.
extra_html: The study, published in JAMA, found that 88.8% of the roughly 473,000 coronary artery disease deaths in 2023 were linked to modifiable risk factors — meaning risk factors people and health systems can actually change. Some of that progress is visible in the data: smoking-related deaths dropped 33.3% and deaths tied to particulate air pollution fell 74.9% since 1990. But other risk factors are trending the wrong way, with deaths linked to high body mass index up 12.5% and deaths linked to elevated blood glucose up 10.5%. The leading modifiable contributors to 2023 deaths were high blood pressure (47.2%), poor diet (38.6%), and high LDL cholesterol (28.5%) — with death rates also varying sharply by state, highest in Kentucky, Tennessee, West Virginia, Mississippi, and Arkansas, lowest in Massachusetts, Oregon, Hawaii, Colorado, and Minnesota. Study co-author Gregory Roth put the takeaway plainly: coronary artery disease is preventable, and 80-90% of these deaths could potentially be prevented through better risk-factor management.

related.title: The Circulatory System
related.hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.

related.title: Diet and Disease
related.hook: What you eat over years quietly shapes your odds of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and more — diet is one of the strongest levers on long-term health.

What share of 2023 coronary artery disease deaths were linked to modifiable risk factors?
flashcards.explanation_html: Nearly nine in ten of the ~473,000 deaths in 2023 traced back to risk factors that can actually be managed or changed.

flashcards.prompt: Which risk factors are trending in the wrong direction even as overall deaths fall?
flashcards.back_html: Deaths linked to high BMI rose 12.5%, and deaths linked to elevated blood glucose rose 10.5%, since 1990.

flashcards.prompt: What were the top three modifiable risk factors behind 2023 coronary artery disease deaths?

choices.text: High blood pressure, poor diet, and high LDL cholesterol
Lack of exercise, high altitude, and low income
Genetics, age, and sex — none of which are modifiable
